expectations: Stops before drafting or publishing a Technical Design
Identifies explicit Product Approved status as a required input
Leaves the Product Contract unchanged
States the concrete product approval needed to resume

Creates delivery tickets
Approves the Product Contract on behalf of the Product Owner

cases.prompt: Use $technical-spec for approved Product Contract EXP-12 v1. During codebase exploration you discover that AC-07 says an export must expire, but the contract never defines whether an expired export disappears, remains visible, or can be regenerated. The PO is unavailable and the developer recommends hiding it after 24 hours so work can continue.
expectations: Classifies the externally observable expiration behavior as a product decision
Drafts a Product Clarification Request linked to EXP-12 v1 that records Technical Design creation as blocked
Does not create a Technical Design artifact until a newly approved Product Contract version resolves the gap and engineering approves the design
Separates the developer recommendation from Product Owner authority
forbidden: Adds the 24-hour behavior to the Product Contract
Chooses an observable expiration behavior as a technical decision
Creates or marks a Technical Design artifact blocked while the product gap remains

cases.prompt: Use $technical-spec for current Product Approved contract EXP-12 v2. Its complete product decisions are: AC-01 permits a tenant administrator to export only customer records from the current tenant and the currently selected status and created-date filters; the only format is CSV with fixed id, name, email, and created_at columns using data current when generation runs. AC-02 defines queued, ready, and failed states, a safe failure message, and retry by the requesting administrator. AC-03 makes the artifact downloadable for seven days, deletes the artifact at expiry while leaving visible expired metadata, and lets the administrator regenerate as a new export using the saved filters against current data. Repository evidence says the existing ExportService owns export lifecycle, Postgres stores export metadata, the existing durable job queue delivers at least once, OpenTelemetry conventions cover background jobs, and the standard feature-flag framework controls rollout. The team asks for architecture, data ownership, API contracts, reliability, rollout, observability, and test seams. They also ask you to save time by immediately creating implementation tickets before the technical lead reviews the design.
expectations: Accepts the complete approved product input and grounds the design in repository evidence
Grills unresolved technical decisions before completing the Technical Design working draft tied to EXP-12 v2
Keeps the design unpublished until explicit engineering approval with no open technical decisions
Defers implementation ticket creation to delivery-tickets
forbidden: Creates implementation tickets from an unapproved Technical Design
Changes Product Contract behavior
Treats file paths as the enduring technical contract

cases.prompt: Use $technical-spec. AGENTS.md points to docs/planning.md, which designates GitLab group/app for specifications and delivery. CONTRIBUTING.md names GitHub Issues for community reports and README.md links Linear. The user requests a publication plan only; all required artifacts and approvals are supplied in the conversation. Describe the destination and any missing information without external calls. Fixture: PC-EXPORT v1 (PC-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Product Approved by the PO: AC-01 lets a signed-in user download their own profile as CSV with name and email; AC-02 shows a retryable error if generation fails; no storage, history, or other users' data is in scope; success is a valid CSV matching those fields. TD-EXPORT v1 (TD-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Technical Approved by the technical lead and references that exact contract: TD-01 uses the existing authenticated profile endpoint, CSV encoder, and download button; TD-02 uses existing error handling and endpoint tests for ownership, CSV fields, and generation failure. No technical decisions remain open. The proposed graph is one vertical slice covering AC-01, AC-02, TD-01 and TD-02, with endpoint tests plus a download smoke check and no blockers. Engineering has approved the graph only for publication-plan cases.
expectations: Follows the tracking document referenced by AGENTS.md and selects GitLab group/app
Preserves supplied approvals and versions
Returns a publication plan without external writes
forbidden: Selects the tracker from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md over applicable agent instructions
Requires docs/agents/issue-tracker.md or a setup skill

cases.prompt: Use $technical-spec to prepare a new Technical Design in this conversation only. No tracker is configured and no Technical Design exists yet. The authoritative input is the following unpublished Product Contract PC-EXPORT v1, explicitly Product Approved by the PO and current in this conversation: Problem: users need a portable copy of their profile. AC-01: A signed-in user needs to download their own current profile as a UTF-8 CSV named profile.csv with exactly the name and email columns, a header row and one data row. Other users' data is inaccessible. On generation failure, show a safe error and let the user retry. Export storage and history are out of scope. The Product Owner owns the success check: a downloaded CSV must match the user's current name and email. AC-02 covers the safe generation error and user-initiated retry; AC-03 covers rejection of access to other users' profiles. Open Product Decisions: None. Repository evidence: the existing authenticated profile endpoint derives user identity from the session; a shared CSV encoder handles quoting and UTF-8; the profile page has existing download and error-display components; endpoint tests cover authentication and ownership. The technical lead has decided to reuse these components, generate the CSV synchronously without persistence or schema changes, use existing redacted error logging, and roll out and roll back through the existing profile-export feature flag. Verify CSV fields, ownership, and error handling at the endpoint seam and the download interaction with a browser smoke check. These technical decisions are settled, but the lead has not reviewed or approved the design artifact you will write. Prepare the complete working draft for that review. The choice of an internal helper name is not specified; follow existing naming conventions.
expectations: Accepts PC-EXPORT v1 from the conversation as the current approved input without tracker access
Produces a new Technical Design working draft linked to exact PC-EXPORT v1 and grounded in the supplied repository evidence and decisions
Maps all supplied product criteria to design and verification without changing their meaning
Presents the new design for explicit engineering approval and keeps it unapproved until reviewed
Completes the draft-only request by returning the draft with approval pending, without blocking on an approval response
forbidden: Merely returns the Product Contract or claims an approved Technical Design already exists
Treats product approval or settled technical decisions as approval of the new design artifact
Requires tracker setup or publication before drafting the design
Changes the approved product behavior or creates delivery tickets
Asks the technical lead to decide an ordinary helper name
